title: Unified Telemetry Router and Alert Noise Harmonizer
creator: Aisha Fernando
description: Build a unified telemetry routing layer that normalizes trace/metric/log signals, deduplicates correlated alerts, and applies policy-driven noise reduction before firing SLO burn-rate and paging rules. This aims to reduce alert fatigue, improve on-call signal-to-noise, and ensure SLO alerts are actionable and attributable to a single root cause when possible.
background: We have multiple sources (request traces, sidecar metrics, ingestion pipelines) producing overlapping signals that trigger separate burn-rate and latency alerts. On-call fatigue and false-positives have risen as we onboard more models and regional serving clusters. Previous attempts to tune thresholds per-service have been brittle and don't scale across multi-tenant Dedicated deployments.
goals: Introduce a lightweight Telemetry Router service that can attach canonical context to incoming spans/metrics/logs (customer_id, model_variant, route, request_tier)
Implement an Alert Harmonizer stage that groups related signals (same trace id, same KV-prefix) to produce a single incident candidate
Surface enriched, deduplicated incidents to the Burn-Rate engine so paging is driven by consolidated, high-fidelity signals
Provide dashboard widgets showing grouped vs raw alert counts and a rollback knob to disable grouping per-customer
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry Router accepts traces/metrics/logs and emits normalized events with canonical tags for at least 75% of production traffic in us-west-2
Alert Harmonizer reduces duplicate alert volume by >= 40% on the pilot service during a 2-week A/B run
No increase in median alert-to-ack latency by more than 10% after harmonization
Burn-rate alerts and paging decisions correlate with grouped incidents in 95% of sampled post-incident reviews
tasks: Design telemetry canonical tagset and mapping rules (trace, metric, log) — design doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Telemetry+Router+Design
Prototype lightweight router (Go) as sidecar-capable service with gRPC ingest and Kafka output
Implement Harmonizer logic (grouping heuristics: trace-id, request_prefix, error_signature) with config flags
Integrate harmonized events with existing Burn-Rate engine and validate policy mapping
Create observability dashboards: grouped-alerts, reduction-rate, false-positive-rate
Run canary on 'generation-api' team and collect two weeks of metrics
Iterate on heuristics and expose per-customer toggles in Console
Write runbook updates and oncall playbook entries
design_notes: Favor deterministic grouping heuristics first (trace-id, span-parent chain) and fall back to probabilistic similarity for orphaned signals
Keep harmonizer stateless for majority paths; use short-lived sidecar caches for in-flight correlation to reduce storage costs
Add an opt-out header for customers that want raw signals for their internal SLO tooling
Expose grouping decisions and confidence score in incident payload so oncall can inspect whether grouping was applied
telemetry: Emit metric: telemetry_router.ingest_rps per-cluster and per-customer
Log structured event with fields: grouped_count, raw_alert_ids, confidence_score
Trace example flows and tag with router.node for end-to-end latency debugging
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Week 0-1): Deploy router in canary mode for generation-api in us-west-2; no harmonization applied, only tagging
Phase 2 (Week 2): Enable Harmonizer at low aggressiveness (only trace-id and span-parent grouping) and monitor grouped_alerts dashboard
Phase 3 (Week 3): Increase aggressiveness (include error-signature hashing) and enable for additional low-traffic tenants
Phase 4 (Week 5): Open beta: expose per-customer toggle in Console and run cross-team training
Rollback: toggle off harmonizer at tenant or cluster level; fallback policy is to route raw alerts to burn-rate engine
monitoring_kpis: Alert volume reduction (%) compared to baseline
Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for grouped incidents
False-positive rate for burn-rate alerts (tracked by periodic postmortems)
risks: Over-grouping may hide concurrent independent failures; mitigated by confidence score and manual override
Increased latency in alert pipeline due to correlation window; mitigated by tight window (200ms) and sidecar caching
Customers relying on raw alerts for internal tooling may be impacted; provide opt-out and thorough communication
Edge cases where trace-id is missing in legacy integrations requiring heuristic fallback
